text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: multiple streaming sessions to customer KestrelPay are unexpectedly closing after ~60s of idle. Affected: enterprise VPC (dedicated-pool-7). Paging SRE rota.

mia: saw it, getting alerted via our gateway health checks. Repro in staging with similar load.

raj: any upstream 502s or proxy resets in the logs?

mia: digging — quick grep shows repeated `upstream reset` from app-proxy at ~60s. Looks like keepalive/idle timeout on their side.

elaine: KestrelPay ops on call says they haven't changed config, but their app gateway has a default 60s idle kill. They're investigating.

tomas: impact: user sessions drop for streaming responses (chat/voice) — visible errors in our logs: `io/stream: client disconnected during recv`. Customer reports partial data loss and retries causing token spikes.

jess: Is this hitting tenant isolation / noisy neighbor? This pool is dedicated to them, but we still see token cost blips because clients retry.

mia: confirmed it's not other tenants. Traffic is all KestrelPay. Dedicated pool CPU/mem fine. Root cause likely app-proxy keepalive.

raj: Mitigation plan: 1) Add server-side periodic pings at 30s to keep the socket alive (we can enable at the gateway layer), 2) Temporarily route affected users to an alternate dedicated instance with extended timeouts, 3) Ask KestrelPay to extend idle timeout to 180s while we validate.

elaine: I'll coordinate with Cust Success to get KestrelPay to flip their config. KestrelOps contact: @kestrel-ops (via support channel) — they're available but need exact steps.

tomas: For step 1: we can enable `ws-heartbeat: true` in the gateway config. Quick patch: 
```
# gateway config snippet
ws_heartbeat:
  enabled: true
  interval_ms: 30000
```
I'll push to canary now.

mia: pushing canary to dedicated-pool-7 now. Rolling to 1/3 nodes. Watch logs: `kubectl -n gateway logs -l pool=dedicated-pool-7 | grep heartbeat`.

raj: Also adding a fallback route rule to send traffic to dedicated-pool-9 with 180s timeout in case canary fails. Config command: `redwood route update --from pool=dedicated-pool-7 --fallback pool=dedicated-pool-9 --timeout 180s`

jess: I'm drafting a brief customer-facing note: "We're seeing streaming disconnects due to idle timeouts on gateway. We're enabling pings and a short fallback route; request you increase idle timeout to 180s." Sending it to KestrelPay now.

elaine: KestrelOps responded: will toggle idle to 180s in 10m and confirm. They asked for the exact header/ping behaviour we use.

mia: canary logs show pings being sent and connections staying open. No increase in token usage observed in the first 5m window.

tomas: OK start routing fallback in 2m. KestrelOps says they'll flip on their side in 8m.

raj: once we have both changes, we'll monitor for 30m then close. If disconnects continue, escalate to infra and consider upgrading NLB idle settings.

jess: oncall handoff note: current oncall SRE is mia. Tomorrow morning handoff to raj at 08:00 UTC — include check: `grep client_disconnected` in gateway logs and confirm KestrelPay timeout change.

oncall-bot: ACTION: set incident status -> mitigation in progress. Incident channel: #incidents. Incident owner: mia.

mia: marking mitigation working. Will update in 15m with metrics (disconnect count, retry rate, token delta).

elaine: Customer confirmed change at 1768005840. KestrelPay: "idle timeout set to 180s, confirming no more disconnects on our side."

mia: metrics update at 1768005900: disconnects dropped from 18/min -> 1/min, retries reduced ~85%. Token spike normalized.

tomas: leaving postmortem notes: action items: 1) add ws-heartbeat as safe default for enterprise appgateways, 2) add automatic fallback routing when persistent websocket disconnects detected, 3) document recommended customer gateway settings (idle timeout >= 120s).

jess: sending incident summary to KestrelPay and scheduling a follow-up call to discuss long-term config.

mia: closing incident in 30m if metrics stable. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
